head_commit.message:
fix(codex): repair the Linux sandbox so keepalive runs can execute commands (#3439)

* fix(codex): repair the Linux sandbox so keepalive runs can execute commands

Every codex keepalive run across the fleet is currently inert. codex's workspace-write
sandbox shells out to bubblewrap, which unshares the network namespace and then brings
up loopback; that needs CAP_NET_ADMIN inside the namespace, and Ubuntu 24.04+ runner
images ship kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, which withholds it. Every
shell command dies before it runs with `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`.

Upstream: openai/codex#14719, #15982, #17337, #19235.

- Best-effort `sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`, which restores
  the sandbox exactly as designed.
- If that is not permitted, retry once with sandbox network access enabled, so bwrap
  shares the host network namespace instead of unsharing it and never attempts the
  loopback setup. Filesystem confinement is unchanged.
- A `bwrap:` line in the session output now forces a non-zero exit. codex exits 0 when its
  sandbox fails, which is why a totally blocked agent read as a successful turn with
  nothing to do -- and is how a run that did nothing wrote a terminal completion record
  and latched the keepalive loop shut (#3433).

Closes #3438

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(codex): report the userns-relaxation outcome in the sandbox line

shellcheck SC2034: the flag was set and never read. It belongs in the diagnostic line
next to the sandbox mode -- when a codex run misbehaves, whether the kernel restriction
was lifted is the first thing worth knowing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(codex): anchor the sandbox detection, scope the sysctl, cover both in tests

All four points from review, each a real defect:

- The detection matched any `bwrap:` text in a capture file that holds codex's --json
  event stream as well as its stderr. An agent_message quoting the error -- including an
  agent working on this very incident -- would have retried a healthy run with a weakened
  sandbox and then forced it to exit 1. Anchored to the start of a line, which every
  stderr line is and no JSON event line can be.
- The apparmor relaxation ran for read-only callers too (the keepalive E2E caller selects
  read-only), disabling a host-wide mitigation for the rest of the runner's life with no
  benefit. Now gated on workspace-write.
- openai/codex#14719 is a multi-agent spawn issue; the Linux sandbox reports are #15982,
  #17337 and #19235. Citations corrected in both places.
- The new shell branches had no coverage. tests/workflows/test_codex_sandbox_startup_failure.py
  runs the workflow's own pattern, read out of the workflow, against a real stderr line and
  against an agent message that quotes it, and pins the anchor, the workspace-write gate,
  the one-shot retry guard, and the forced non-zero exit.

Deliberate-break gate: removing the `^` anchor fails
test_does_not_fire_on_an_agent_message_that_quotes_the_error and
test_the_pattern_is_anchored; restoring it passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: stranske <tim@stranskemo.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
